source.anchor: Original Samplinglib path-law transport supplement: Continuous paths give vanishing transport cost
source.original_text:
Let \(T\) be a first-countable topological space, \(\Omega\) a measurable space, and \(E\) a compact topological space with a measurable structure for which every open subset of \(E\times E\) is measurable in the product sigma algebra. Let \(P\) be a probability law on \(\Omega\), and let \(X_t:\Omega\to E\) be measurable for every \(t\in T\). Assume that, on one event of full probability, \(t\mapsto X_t\) is continuous on all of \(T\). Write \(\mu_t=(X_t)_\#P\). Let \(c:E\times E\to[0,\infty)\) be a continuous finite cost with \(c(x,x)=0\) for every \(x\). For every fixed \(s\in T\), the Kantorovich cost with cost \(c\) from \(\mu_t\) to \(\mu_s\) tends to zero as \(t\to s\). The limit is in the extended nonnegative reals.

\(T\) is first-countable. \(E\) is compact; its product topology has measurable open sets in the product sigma algebra.
\(P\) is a probability law, every time slice \(X_t\) is measurable, and entire paths are continuous on a single event of full probability.
The continuous cost \(c\) takes values in the finite nonnegative reals and vanishes on the diagonal.

\mathsf C_c(\mu,\nu):=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\int c\,d\pi,\qquad \mathsf C_c(\mu_t,\mu_s)\longrightarrow0\quad(t\to s).

theorem anonymous_target.{u_1, u_2,
    u_3}
  {T : Type u_1} {Ω : Type u_2} {E : Type u_3} [TopologicalSpace T] [FirstCountableTopology T] [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  [TopologicalSpace E] [CompactSpace E] [MeasurableSpace E] [OpensMeasurableSpace (E × E)]
  (P : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (X : T → Ω → E) (hX : ∀ (t : T), Measurable (X t))
  (hpaths : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂↑P, Continuous fun t => X t ω) (c : C(E × E, NNReal)) (hzero : ∀ (x : E), c (x, x) = 0)
  (s : T) :
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun t =>
      AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.Transport.transportCost (fun z => ↑(c z))
        ↑(P.map (Measurable.aemeasurable (hX t))) ↑(P.map (Measurable.aemeasurable (hX s))))
    (nhds s) (nhds 0)

blind_reconstruction.text:
Objects: For measures μ and ν on E, a coupling is exactly a measure γ on E×E whose first and second projection pushforwards are μ and ν. For κ:E×E→[0,∞], define C_κ(μ,ν)=inf{∫⁻ κ(z) dγ(z) : γ is such a coupling}. This is the infimum in the extended nonnegative reals; an empty feasible set has infimum ∞. The supplied definition imposes no additional condition on γ and makes no assertion that the infimum is attained. Write μ_t=(X(t,·))#P. This map function is determined by the explicitly supplied measurable proof hX(t), including hX(p.1) and hX(q.1) when product points are used. In this target κ(z) is c(z) coerced from the finite nonnegative reals into [0,∞].

Domains: T is an arbitrary topological space with a first-countable topology. Ω is a measurable space and P is a probability measure on Ω. E is a compact topological space equipped with a measurable space, with the assumption that every open subset of the topological product E×E is measurable for its product measurable structure. No equality of the measurable structure with the Borel structure, Hausdorff condition, metrizability, or first-countability of E is stated. X:T→Ω→E and c:E×E→[0,∞) is a continuous map taking finite nonnegative-real values. A point s∈T is specified. No measurable structure on T and no topological structure on Ω is required.

Quantifiers: Universally quantify T, Ω, E and all the listed structures, then P and X. Assume measurability of X(t,·) for every t and the one almost-sure path-continuity condition. Universally choose the continuous c, assume c(x,x)=0 for every x∈E, and choose any s∈T. For each such set of data the asserted neighborhood-filter limit holds.

Assumptions: For every t∈T, X(t,·):Ω→E is measurable. For P-almost every ω, the entire map t↦X(t,ω) is continuous on T. The finite nonnegative cost c is continuous on E×E and satisfies c(x,x)=0 for all x∈E. The compactness, first-countability and product-open-set measurability assumptions are exactly those in the domains slot. No joint measurability of (t,ω)↦X(t,ω), symmetry or triangle inequality for c, or separation property c(x,y)=0⇒x=y is assumed.

Conclusion: As t tends to s in T, C_c(μ_t,μ_s) tends to 0 in [0,∞], where c is coerced into the extended nonnegative reals in the nonnegative integral. Precisely, t↦C_c((X(t,·))#P,(X(s,·))#P sends the neighborhood filter of s to the neighborhood filter of 0 in the extended nonnegative reals.

Scopes: This is a topological limit of deterministic extended-nonnegative transport-cost values for each specified s, not an almost-sure limit of random variables. The path-continuity assumption is one P-almost-everywhere statement asserting continuity on all of T. Slice measurability is required for every t and the diagonal cost identity for every state. There is no finite time horizon, no restriction to an ordered time set, and no uniform-in-s convergence conclusion. No metric or Wasserstein interpretation of this general cost is asserted.

Constant dependencies: No numerical bound, rate, modulus, or existential constant is part of the statement. The limit depends on the selected P, X, c, spaces and base point s; the theorem asserts the limit separately for every such choice.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.Transport
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.WeakDiffusionLaw
import Mathlib.Analysis.Real.Sqrt

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.PathLawTransport

open Filter MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal NNReal Topology
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.Transport
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.WeakDiffusionLaw

variable {T Ω E : Type*} [TopologicalSpace T] [FirstCountableTopology T]
  [MeasurableSpace Ω] [TopologicalSpace E] [CompactSpace E] [MeasurableSpace E]
  [OpensMeasurableSpace (E × E)]

/-- Same-sample couplings of two evaluations of a continuous path have
cost tending to zero as the first time approaches the second. -/
theorem tendsto_transportCost_marginal_of_ae_continuous
    (P : ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (X : T → Ω → E) (hX : ∀ t, Measurable (X t))
    (hpaths : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), Continuous (fun t => X t ω))
    (c : C(E × E, ℝ≥0)) (hzero : ∀ x : E, c (x, x) = 0) (s : T) :
    Tendsto (fun t => transportCost (fun z => (c z : ℝ≥0∞))
      (P.map (hX t).aemeasurable : Measure E) (P.map (hX s).aemeasurable : Measure E))
      (𝓝 s) (𝓝 0) := by
  let Z (t : T) (ω : Ω) := (X t ω, X s ω)
  have hZ (t : T) : Measurable (Z t) := (hX t).prodMk (hX s)
  have hZpaths : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), Continuous (fun t => Z t ω) :=
    hpaths.mono fun _ hω => hω.prodMk continuous_const
  let γ (t : T) := P.map (hZ t).aemeasurable
  have hγ : Continuous γ := continuous_marginal_law_of_ae_continuous P Z hZ hZpaths
  let C (t : T) := ∫⁻ z, (c z : ℝ≥0∞) ∂(γ t : Measure (E × E))
  have hC : Continuous C := (ProbabilityMeasure.continuous_lintegral_continuousMap c).comp hγ
  have hCs : C s = 0 := by
    dsimp [C, γ]
    have hc : Measurable (fun z : E × E => (c z : ℝ≥0∞)) :=
      measurable_coe_nnreal_ennreal.comp c.continuous.measurable
    rw [lintegral_map hc (hZ s)]
    simp [Z, hzero]
  have hlim : Tendsto C (𝓝 s) (𝓝 0) := hCs ▸ hC.continuousAt
  refine tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le tendsto_const_nhds hlim (fun _ => bot_le) ?_
  intro t
  apply transportCost_le_lintegral_of_isCoupling
  constructor
  · simp only [γ, ProbabilityMeasure.toMeasure_map, Z, Measure.fst_map_prodMk (hX s)]
  · simp only [γ, ProbabilityMeasure.toMeasure_map, Z, Measure.snd_map_prodMk (hX t)]

/-- A transport and pointwise estimate gives joint continuity of a field
along the marginal laws of an almost surely continuous process. -/
theorem continuous_of_path_law_transport_bound
    {F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup F]
    (P : ProbabilityMeasure Ω) (X : T → Ω → E) (hX : ∀ t, Measurable (X t))
    (hpaths : ∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure Ω), Continuous (fun t => X t ω))
    (c : C(E × E, ℝ≥0)) (hzero : ∀ x : E, c (x, x) = 0)
    (U : T × E → F) (L : ℝ)
    (hbound : ∀ p q : T × E, ‖U p - U q‖ ≤ L *
      (Real.sqrt (transportCost (fun z => ((c z : ℝ≥0∞) ^ 2))
        (P.map (hX p.1).aemeasurable : Measure E)
        (P.map (hX q.1).aemeasurable : Measure E)).toReal + (c (p.2, q.2) : ℝ))) :
    Continuous U := by
  rw [continuous_iff_continuousAt]
  intro q
  rw [ContinuousAt, tendsto_iff_norm_sub_tendsto_zero]
  let Q (p : T × E) := transportCost (fun z => ((c z : ℝ≥0∞) ^ 2))
    (P.map (hX p.1).aemeasurable : Measure E) (P.map (hX q.1).aemeasurable : Measure E)
  let c₂ : C(E × E, ℝ≥0) := c ^ 2
  have hzero₂ (x : E) : c₂ (x, x) = 0 := by simp [c₂, hzero]
  have hQ : Tendsto Q (𝓝 q) (𝓝 0) := by
    have h := (tendsto_transportCost_marginal_of_ae_continuous P X hX hpaths c₂ hzero₂ q.1).comp
      continuous_fst.continuousAt
    simpa only [Q, c₂, Function.comp_def, ContinuousMap.pow_apply, ENNReal.coe_pow] using h
  have hroot : Tendsto (fun p => Real.sqrt (Q p).toReal) (𝓝 q) (𝓝 0) := by
    simpa only [Function.comp_def, ENNReal.toReal_zero, Real.sqrt_zero] using
      ((ENNReal.tendsto_toReal ENNReal.zero_ne_top).comp hQ).sqrt
  have hc : Continuous (fun p : T × E => (c (p.2, q.2) : ℝ)) :=
    NNReal.continuous_coe.comp (c.continuous.comp (continuous_snd.prodMk continuous_const))
  have hpoint : Tendsto (fun p : T × E => (c (p.2, q.2) : ℝ)) (𝓝 q) (𝓝 0) := by
    simpa only [hzero, NNReal.coe_zero] using (hc.continuousAt (x := q)).tendsto
  have hmajor : Tendsto (fun p => L * (Real.sqrt (Q p).toReal + (c (p.2, q.2) : ℝ)))
      (𝓝 q) (𝓝 0) := by
    simpa only [add_zero, mul_zero] using tendsto_const_nhds.mul (hroot.add hpoint)
  exact tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le tendsto_const_nhds hmajor
    (fun _ => norm_nonneg _) (fun p => hbound p q)

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Measure.PathLawTransport

steps.title: Use the same sample at two times
steps.text: The paired process \(Z_t=(X_t,X_s)\) has continuous sample paths on the original full event. The marginal-law theorem therefore makes \(\gamma_t=(Z_t)_\#P\) weakly continuous. Its two marginals are \(\mu_t,\mu_s\).
